residual_1_oq1_set_based_status: RESOLVED — and the rule is now FULLY SOUND. The hard error is re-keyed onto the SET W_X of ALL prior same-block SharedWrite indices to id X since the last barrier (a HirStmt::Barrier clears the set), NOT just the most-recent write (A.4.1 rewritten, typecheck.rs item 5 rewritten, coder_handoff_notes OQ1 entry rewritten, AT-1636 extended, edge_cases entry rewritten, open_questions OQ1 rewritten). The precise rule checks ProvablyEqual FIRST: (1) ProvablyEqual to ANY w_k in W_X -> NO diagnostic (self-RAW); (2) else ProvablyDisequal to EVERY w_k in W_X -> HARD ERROR; (3) else -> advisory warning. The r2 residual `tile[0u32]=a; tile[1u32]=b; let w=tile[0u32];` is now NO diagnostic: r=IntLit(0) is ProvablyEqual to the RETAINED `tile[0u32]=a` write (W_X={0,1}, the equality short-circuits before the disequality-to-all test ever runs). Confirmed against AT-1636(b) which locks exactly this case. The data-structure change (Vec<index-expr> per id, cleared by a barrier, instead of Option<most-recent>) is the ONLY change and is implementable with the SAME expr.rs leaf machinery already verified in r2 (BindingId Eq / IntLit value / GidBuiltin axis).
oq1_soundness_confirmation: FULLY SOUND — no remaining correct-kernel false positive constructible. The hard error fires iff the read index is ProvablyDisequal to EVERY prior same-block write since the last barrier — which provably means THIS invocation never wrote that slot, so the read is necessarily either (a) a genuine cross-invocation access that REQUIRES a barrier (missing -> the NVIDIA-passes/AMD-races trap, correctly rejected) or (b) an uninitialized read in a single-invocation kernel (buggy regardless of any barrier). Both are incorrect kernels. Adversarial correct patterns probed, ALL avoid the hard error: (A) `tile[i]=v; tile[j]=w; read tile[i]` (i,j distinct dynamic params) -> r=i ProvablyEqual to the tile[i] write (same LocalRead BindingId, no reassignment between) -> NO diagnostic, regardless of j. (B) `tile[i]=v; tile[i+1]=w; read tile[i]` -> ProvablyEqual to the tile[i] write short-circuits before the Unknown(i+1 vs i) is even consulted -> NO diagnostic. (C) `tile[i]=v;` in a loop, then a barrier, then `read tile[i]` after the barrier -> the barrier CLEARS W_X so there is no same-block prior write to pair the read against -> NO hard error (and the loop-carried/cross-block write is advisory-only by construction). (D) `tile[gid(0)]=v; read tile[gid(0)]` -> both GidBuiltin axis 0 -> ProvablyEqual -> NO diagnostic. (E) `tile[2]=a; tile[5]=b; read tile[2]; read tile[5]` -> each read ProvablyEqual to its own prior write -> NO diagnostic. (F) reassignment `tile[i]=v; i=i+1; read tile[i]` -> same BindingId but binding reassigned between -> NOT ProvablyEqual, NOT ProvablyDisequal -> Unknown -> ADVISORY WARNING only (never a hard error; and this pattern IS genuinely suspicious, so the warning is appropriate, not a false positive). The ProvablyDisequal predicate is conservative (only genuinely-distinct constants / distinct GidBuiltin axes; distinct dynamic bindings are Unknown, NOT ProvablyDisequal), so two distinct dynamic indices never trigger the hard error. I cannot construct a correct kernel that reads a slot it never wrote (in the same block, no barrier) — that is by definition a bug. The single-invocation uninitialized-read hard-error is acceptably documented in A.4.1, the edge_cases entry, the open_questions OQ1 resolution, and the DESIGN.md additions: it rejects an already-incorrect kernel (a barrier would not make it correct); only the diagnostic NAME is slightly off (says 'missing barrier' when the true bug is an uninitialized read), explicitly flagged as cosmetic, not a soundness hole. The architect's stated soundness property — 'the hard error fires on NO correct kernel' — now HOLDS.

summary: FINAL CONFIRM (r3) of the M3.2 design, scoped to the TWO residuals the r2 review left open. BOTH are RESOLVED and the OQ1 rule is now FULLY SOUND -> APPROVE (unblocks coding). (1) OQ1 set-based fix: the missing-barrier hard error is re-keyed from the MOST-RECENT write onto the SET W_X of ALL prior same-block writes to the id since the last barrier (ProvablyEqual to ANY -> no diagnostic, checked first; ProvablyDisequal to EVERY -> hard error; else -> advisory warning; a barrier clears the set). The r2 residual `tile[0]=a; tile[1]=b; let w=tile[0];` is now NO diagnostic (read 0 ProvablyEqual to the retained tile[0]=a write), locked by AT-1636(b). I probed multiple adversarial correct patterns — distinct-param two-slot writes read-back-i, i+1-offset write, write-loop-then-barrier-then-read, gid-self-read, multi-constant slots, and a reassigned-binding read — ALL avoid the hard error (self-reads are ProvablyEqual short-circuited; the reassigned-binding case demotes to advisory, not a hard error). The hard error now fires ONLY when the read is ProvablyDisequal to EVERY prior write, i.e. provably a slot this invocation never wrote, which is necessarily a genuine cross-invocation missing-barrier OR a single-invocation uninitialized read — both incorrect kernels. No correct-kernel false positive is constructible; the 'fires on no correct kernel' property holds. The single-invocation uninitialized-read hard-error is acceptably documented (rejects an already-buggy kernel; only the diagnostic name is cosmetically off). (2) AT-429 test edit: typecheck.rs:4393 is added to files_to_modify and is a first-class acceptance test, assertion inverted to expect BarrierInDivergentContext, test renamed; CONFIRMED (by workspace grep) it is the ONLY barrier-in-conditional site — examples/workgroup_barrier_demo.axc has its barrier at top level (if-body has none), so nothing else regresses. (3) No-regression: r3 added EXACTLY two changelog entries (r3 OQ1 set-of-writes, r3 OQ2 AT-429) and left all 4 CRITICAL fixes, the C1-not-FA2 relabel, the coopmat-from-Workgroup-storage path, and the OQ2 conditional_depth mechanism textually intact; the only edits are A.4.1 (set-based), typecheck.rs item 5 + new item 7, AT-1636(b), and the added AT-429. Implementability is a Vec<index-expr>-per-id swap using the same expr.rs leaf machinery already verified. No new holes. APPROVE.
